summary: This Wikipedia-derived note surveys Melbourne, Australia, covering its universities and their rankings, its founding and gold-rush growth, water supply management, media and television production, sport events, housing, environmental and water issues, rail and transport, economic growth, and radio stations. It presents Melbourne as a major education, sporting, media and transport hub with a history tied to the 1850s gold rush.
one_line: An overview of Melbourne, Australia's education, history, water supply, media, sport, housing, transport and radio landscape.
key_facts: The discovery of gold in Victoria in mid 1851 led to the Victorian gold rush, and Melbourne experienced rapid growth.
By 1865, Melbourne had overtaken Sydney as Australia's most populous city.
Melbourne was founded by free settlers from Van Diemen's Land on 30 August 1835.
Melbourne was named by Governor of New South Wales Sir Richard Bourke after British Prime Minister William Lamb, 2nd Viscount Melbourne.
Queen Victoria officially declared Melbourne a city in 1847.
Melbourne served as the nation's interim seat of government after federation in 1901 until 1927.
The Thomson River Dam, in the Victorian Alps, can hold around 60% of Melbourne's water capacity.
The Wonthaggi desalination plant was announced in June 2007 at a cost of $3.1 billion, capable of treating 150 billion litres of water per year.
Flinders Street Station was the world's busiest passenger station in 1926.
The Melbourne rail network recorded 232.0 million passenger trips in the 2013–2014 financial year, its highest ever.
Melbourne Airport (Tullamarine Airport) is the second busiest airport in Australia.
Melbourne hosted the 1956 Summer Olympic Games, the first Olympics held in the southern hemisphere and Oceania.
Melbourne was the southernmost city to host the Commonwealth Games, in 2006.
Melbourne is home to seven public universities, including the University of Melbourne and Monash University.
Melbourne was ranked the world's fourth top university city in 2008 in a poll commissioned by RMIT.
